scope: Device-local ordinary checkout trolley persistence across reloads and application restarts
sourceFixSummary: Unfinished ordinary checkout drafts are saved to this device's SQLite settings with a synchronous WebView mirror; no MariaDB dependency or cross-till draft sync is introduced.
Revisioned null tombstones and atomic SQLite compare-and-swap prevent older queued or old-WebView saves from reviving a cleared trolley.

Cart lines, selected line, customer reference, manual discount reference and recovery identities are retained. Tender, payment modal/method, employee credentials and customer financial balances are excluded.
Validation rejects malformed snapshots without overwriting them; persistence failures remain visible and retryable.
Checkout startup and save boundaries check committed sale/hold ownership before allowing recovery or new checkout activity.
Three startup NULL-normalization migrations now avoid updating already-normalized rows while preserving legacy empty/NULL repair, avoiding unnecessary catalogue/FTS update cascades.
The isolated QA allow-list now includes the checkout boundary checkpoints used by these scenarios; the refreshed full automated checks and normal non-QA build passed after this harness correction.
automatedRefreshReason: Startup migration predicates/tests and the isolated QA checkpoint allow-list/test were added after the first automated snapshot. Final full checks and normal artifact proof were refreshed successfully after the corrected QA build.

nativeCases.title: Ordinary trolley survives page reload
nativeCases.expected: The same unpaid cart lines, quantities, prices and selected line return after a genuine native WebView reload.
observations: Native reload restored exactly two unpaid lines: weighted line 374 pence, quantity 1, note 1500g with quantityLocked/skipStockAdjustment flags; regular line temporary price 225 pence, quantity 3.
The restored trolley showed 4 total items and 1049 pence total; the same QA customer remained selected.

nativeCases.title: Ordinary trolley survives full application quit and restart
nativeCases.expected: Quit the isolated native app, reopen it, complete normal staff authentication and recover the same unfinished trolley without MariaDB.
observations: The native operator genuinely quit the isolated app with Cmd+Q, reopened it and used normal staff PIN authentication.
The exact same two-line trolley returned with 4 total items and 1049 pence total, without MariaDB.

nativeCases.title: Customer is retained; cash tender and payment state reset
nativeCases.expected: After reload/restart, the customer/discount references remain while payment stays closed and cash tender starts empty/zero instead of resuming a payment.
observations: The same QA customer remained selected after native reload and full application restart.
The pre-reload partially entered cash tender of 500 pence was reset to 0. Payment was closed and no sale/payment resumed automatically.
This native case proves the customer/tender behavior; manual discount-reference round-trip is separately covered by the automated journal tests.

nativeCases.title: Cleared trolley does not return after reload
nativeCases.expected: Use the genuine Clear action and confirmation, then reload; the cart remains empty and its null tombstone is preserved.
observations: The native operator used the genuine Clear action and confirmation.
SQLite contained a revisioned null tombstone; after actual native reload the trolley remained empty.

nativeCases.title: Completed cash sale is not restored or charged twice
nativeCases.expected: Complete an isolated mock cash sale, reload and confirm an empty trolley with exactly one saved receipt/payment.
observations: Initial native attempt durably committed an isolated mock cash sale of 169 pence, verified in SQLite, then hit an unknown QA checkpoint error before normal UI cleanup.
This was a QA-only harness allow-list omission, not an unsupported normal-app checkpoint: normal builds compile checkpoints as no-ops.
The missing checkout boundary points and an allow-list unit test have been added; the corrected isolated QA build passed.
On reopening the corrected native app, saved receipt evidence recognized the earlier durably committed sale: the trolley was empty and its stale journal was cleared rather than restored.
Clean native repeat succeeded with the sale-complete modal: receipt cd36370d-3878-405d-a26f-a2659e966de6 saved a 169-pence cash sale.
Actual native reload then showed an empty trolley and a null draft tombstone; the completed trolley was not revived.

nativeCases.title: Hold, retrieve and re-hold retain single trolley ownership
nativeCases.expected: A saved hold does not also revive as an ordinary draft; retrieved hold recovery and re-hold preserve one recoverable copy without loss or duplication.
observations: Created isolated hold 264b4aad-af8d-40eb-a82d-444cbc72033a with status hold and amount 169 pence; the main trolley became empty.
Actual reload remained empty with exactly one held trolley, not a duplicate ordinary draft; genuine Retrieve restored the exact held trolley.
After confirmed full Cmd+Q quit and reopen, the real held-claim recovery prompt appeared and did not automatically process a payment.
Recover saved trolley restored 169 pence. Re-hold created f2390cec-2d62-4fc1-a7c8-f6b7dc427916 while keeping exactly one held trolley.
A fresh ordinary draft cd29a193-635d-4831-8d13-be96256ef757 had empty pendingHoldId and saleIds, and returned after reload while the one held trolley remained separate.

nativeCases.title: Restart after durable sale commit does not revive its stale draft
nativeCases.expected: At the isolated QA checkpoint after the real sale commit but before UI cleanup, quit/restart and verify committed receipt evidence suppresses stale draft recovery.
observations: Armed the genuine isolated after-sale-commit delay checkpoint. SQLite held exactly one completed receipt 09fb274b-53cf-49dc-aba9-592083e52407 while the nonempty draft still referenced that receipt.

Normal Cmd+Q was blocked by the active payment-save guard. The native operator validated and terminated only isolated QA process PID 76912 to simulate a crash; the original POS process was not targeted.
After process termination, durable receipt evidence and the still-nonempty draft were confirmed.
The first forced-restart launch briefly showed a blank native renderer. A clean quit/relaunch, without editing the database, returned normal staff sign-in.
After normal authentication the trolley was empty (0 items); the draft was null and the exact committed receipt remained one row. No completed sale trolley was revived.
limitations: The first launch after forced termination needed one clean relaunch following a blank renderer; its cause was not established and seamless first-launch crash recovery is not claimed.

nativeCases.title: Rejected hold before commit preserves the unpaid trolley
nativeCases.expected: Reject the isolated pre-commit hold checkpoint; no hold is saved, the draft remains retryable, and the same unpaid trolley returns on reload/restart.
observations: The genuine isolated before-hold-commit Reject checkpoint was entered and rejected, verified by native diagnostic proof.
The native error left the unpaid 169-pence trolley intact. The pending-hold marker was cleared and the existing held count remained exactly one.
Actual native reload restored the same one-item 169-pence unpaid ordinary trolley, with the existing held trolley unchanged and no false held tombstone or recovery block.

limits: The originally disappeared RAM-only trolley has not been reconstructed. This fix protects newly saved unfinished trolleys.
The original application, original trolley, provider keys, registrations and live business data were not test targets.

The first cold launch after controlled process termination briefly showed a blank renderer and needed a clean quit/relaunch without database edits. Its cause was not established; seamless first-launch crash recovery is not claimed.
Manual discount-reference round-trip was automated-only because this native mock profile had no active manual discount.
Startup repair SQL tests use an SQLite table mirror to prove no-op update/repair behavior; they do not exercise the actual FTS5 tokenizer.
The native transactions were isolated mock cash/hold records, not real card transactions. No automatic payment resume or live provider calls were used; MariaDB was not needed for draft recovery.
Windows/WebView2, physical card terminals, printers and drawers remain untested by this macOS mock-data exercise.
No release or Windows artifact is certified by the normal macOS arm64 debug build. External-fixture test skips and filters are not claimed as passes.
Final isolated QA state is empty ordinary checkout with one retained mock held trolley and three completed 169-pence mock cash receipts; test records were not removed.
